maya.name: Maya
signals: followed several new classmates this week
gaming club once · lives on campus

steps.label: THE PREDICTION
steps.title: Could an app predict you surprisingly well?
steps.lead: Make the bet before we explain anything.
choices: PROVE IT — an app could predict me pretty well
NO CHANCE — it would get important things about me wrong

runbook.say: Make the bet before we explain anything.
runbook.transition: Keep your answer. We are coming back to it.

steps.label: DIGITAL SHADOW
steps.title: You watched three videos about running shoes.
steps.lead: What does the system actually know?

teachReveal.headline: Only one is directly observed.
teachReveal.explanation: The rest are interpretations. DATA is not the same as MEANING.

runbook.say: What did the system see versus infer?

steps.label: TEACH THE SYSTEM
steps.title: AI is not magic. It is a system.
steps.lead: Phones down. Trace a recommendation through five parts.
flow: DECISION / ACTION — click, buy, watch, share
examples: Spotify: songs played → pattern → Discover Weekly → listen or skip
TikTok: watch time → ranking → For You video → keep scrolling
Netflix: watch history → similarity → recommendation → play or ignore

runbook.say: Slow AI down and it becomes a system we can inspect.
runbook.ask: When does an output become consequential?

steps.label: BE THE ALGORITHM
steps.title: Which three clues should Viking Feed trust most?
steps.lead: Talk with your group first. Choose only three.

runbook.say: You are Viking Feed. Decide which three clues deserve influence.
runbook.ask: What assumption sits behind your choice?

steps.label: SHIP THE OUTPUT
steps.title: What should Viking Feed recommend to Maya?

runbook.ask: What does Viking Feed send Maya?

steps.label: REVEAL + DEBATE
steps.title: The class has spoken. Defend the minority.
steps.lead: Phones down. The winning answer is less interesting than the reasoning.
teachableMoments: Gaming club once does not equal gamer.
Two pizza orders do not equal pizza preference.
Following classmates does not prove extroversion.
Late-night activity does not tell us why Maya was awake.

runbook.say: Someone defend the least popular choice.
runbook.ask: What did we infer that Maya never said?
runbook.reminder: DATA is not the same as MEANING.

steps.label: THE PLOT TWIST
steps.title: Same Maya. New context.
steps.lead: Do not vote yet. Notice when your thinking moves.

reveals.text: Gaming club happened because Maya's roommate asked her to go.
reveals.question: What assumption weakened?

reveals.text: Maya has been looking for ways to meet people outside her residence hall.
reveals.question: What became more plausible?

reveals.text: Maya has a major exam at 8 AM tomorrow.
reveals.question: Which old signals matter less?

runbook.say: Three facts, one at a time. Do not submit anything.

steps.label: VOTE AGAIN
steps.title: What should Viking Feed recommend now?

runbook.say: Changing your mind is updating from better information.
runbook.ask: What should Viking Feed recommend now?

steps.label: SHIFT
steps.title: The room moved.
steps.lead: Watch what happened when context changed.
steps.hero: The algorithm didn't change. The information did.

runbook.say: How many people moved after evidence changed?
runbook.ask: What changed across the five-part system?

steps.label: BREAK THE ALGORITHM
steps.title: Where can the failure enter?
steps.lead: More than one answer can be defensible.
choices: DATA — missing, wrong, or biased information
MODEL / TOOL — bad patterns or wrong objective
failureExamples: The model optimizes clicks instead of wellbeing.
A recommendation keeps Maya awake before an exam.

runbook.ask: Choose a risk and defend another too.

steps.label: 97% MATCH
steps.title: 97% MATCH
choices: No — the number tells me almost nothing

teachReveal.headline: 97% match with what?
teachReveal.explanation: Precision can create authority without telling you what was measured, how reliable it is, or whether the decision is appropriate.

steps.label: CALLBACK
steps.title: Would you make the same bet now?
choices: PROVE IT — AI can predict patterns in my behavior
NO CHANCE — prediction is not the same as understanding me

runbook.say: I am not looking for the same answer. I am looking for a better reason.
runbook.ask: Would you make the same bet now?

steps.label: EXIT
steps.title: Finish one sentence.
steps.lead: Before today, I thought AI prediction was… Now I think… because…
steps.placeholder: Before today… Now I think… because…

runbook.say: Give me one sentence that shows what changed.
runbook.ask: Before today… Now I think… because…
runbook.reminder: This is the only typed response.
